# How This Portfolio Works

*Instructor-owned reference. Do not edit this file: it is the same in every
student's repository. See the legend below for what else is reference-only
versus yours to edit.*

## What this repository is

Your individual engineering portfolio for MMAE 477. Over the semester it
becomes the record of a drone design: requirements, analysis, fabrication,
and validation. Grading reads this repository directly, or a link to it from
Canvas. By the end it should read as a project you'd be glad to show outside
the course.

## This repository is a work in progress, deliberately

The course is running for the first time, and not every deliverable is
locked yet. Rather than pre-populate a full semester's worth of folders
against a plan that may still change, this repository starts minimal and
grows. New folders and documents arrive over the semester as each part of
the plan firms up.

**How updates reach you.** New content is pushed to the course's template
repository, not to your repository directly, your repo has no ongoing
connection to it after you generated it. To pull in an update, once it's
announced, run this in your local clone:

The first time only:
```
git remote add upstream https://github.com/iit-mmae477-479/portfolio-template.git
```

Every time an update is announced:
```
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main --allow-unrelated-histories
git push
```

(Drop `--allow-unrelated-histories` after the first successful merge, it's
only needed once.) This only ever adds or updates files, it never touches
anything you've already committed elsewhere in your repo, unless you've
edited a file marked reference-only below, in which case you may see a
merge conflict. That's the one reason the legend matters.

## What's reference-only, and what's yours

| Item | Reference (do not edit) | Yours (edit freely) |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | | ✓ your front page |
| `PORTFOLIO-GUIDE.md` | ✓ this file | |
| `DECISIONS.md` | | ✓ add rows as you decide things |
| `reference/` | ✓ everything in it | |
| Numbered exercise/lab folders | their `README.md` | everything else inside |

The pattern: any file that's the same across every student's repo is
reference-only. Anything that holds your own work, your name, your
decisions, your analysis, is yours.

**Not sure what "good" looks like?** See
[`reference/worked-example.md`](reference/worked-example.md): a filled-out
summary, decision rows, and requirements, done on a deliberately different
product so the form transfers but the content can't be copied.

## Working rules

1. **Commit regularly.** Commit history is the record of your work, and
   timestamps matter for any late policy.
2. **Commit messages say what changed:** `sizing-exercise: track A, first pass`.
3. **Raw data is immutable.** Once recorded, it's never edited, analysis
   reads from it, it doesn't rewrite it.
4. **No files over 25 MB, no video.** Link large media instead.
5. **Every number is traceable** to a calculation, a measurement, or a
   source, cited where the number appears.

## How grading works

Deliverables are submitted on Canvas, usually as a link to the relevant
commit or file in this repository. The schedule and weighting live on
Canvas, not here, since both may still change.

## Repo setup (done once)

Generated from the course template using **Use this template**: a private
repo under your own account, with instructors added as collaborators. The
repo is yours. You keep it after the course, and after the semester ends you
may make it public.
